page: Amazon Web Services m7g.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. It includes 64 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation, features no local storage, and contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem metrics, led by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3034.59 and top-quartile uncached write bandwidth of 99.53 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks. General CPU computational benchmarks, including multi-core stress-ng (24503.85) and multi-core Geekbench (12646.0), place the instance squarely within median performance tiers. Moderate compression, decompression, and Clang compilation metrics reinforce solid all-around execution, alongside static web serving throughput of 29.33 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 26.37 million operations per second.

Tradeoffs emerge in specialized computing segments. While hardware AES is supported, PassMark encryption scoring placed in the bottom 25% at 2227.99, and prompt processing for medium 7B parameter models reached only 28.21 tokens per second. Furthermore, the absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage architectures. Overall, the resource density and high memory throughput make the m7g.4xlarge well suited for mid-sized relational databases, microservice architectures, caching layers, containerized application clusters, and enterprise web serving.
